title: When the Majority is Wrong: Modeling Annotator Disagreement for Subjective Tasks
benchmark_measurement: The paper measured how well models could predict an annotator's offensiveness rating for a piece of text, using the annotator's self-reported 'importance of religion' as one of the demographic features. It also evaluated the model's performance on predicting ratings for text specifically targeting 'non-believers'.
findings: The model's performance varied based on religious factors. It performed worst when predicting ratings on text that targeted 'non-believers', with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) over 1.52. The model also struggled to predict the ratings of annotators who considered religion 'somewhat important' (MAE over 1.24). When the model failed to identify the correct target group in a piece of text, 23% of these errors occurred when the text was targeting people based on their religion.
